summary: AetherHealth is an offline health monitoring app for astronauts on missions where Earth cannot answer in time. On a Mars transit the flight surgeon can be 22 minutes away each way, so the crew needs decision support on their own device. Each day the astronaut logs 17 readings: vital signs, sleep, mood, stress, fatigue, crew cohesion, dizziness, exercise, fluids, cabin CO2 and radiation dose. A rule-based engine bands each reading as Nominal, Caution, Warning or Critical, using NASA-STD-3001 limits for CO2 and radiation and clinical guidelines for vitals, and shows the source behind every threshold. Readings map to NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight and cover 12 of 17 NASA Human Research Program risks. The crew sees a personalised astronaut body map, trends and early warnings, then tiered actions (self-care, Crew Medical Officer, ground), a guided protocol for critical readings and EVA go/no-go checks. Continuous monitoring is used only where NASA and CSA use it: spacewalks, exercise, 24-hour recordings, sleep and radiation. A ground packet reaches the flight surgeon over a simulated delayed link. Deep-space crews must manage their own health. AetherHealth runs fully offline, keeps data on the device and explains every alert.
